title: OOM breadcrumbs: kernel logs, lib mismatch, quick repro steps
summary: Working notes capturing a recent VM where intermittent GPU OOMs correlated with mixed libcuda/cuda runtime versions and a kernel dmesg pattern; commands tried and suggestions for next steps.
content:
Context: intermittent OOMs observed on model-serving VM pool (g4dn-like). Symptoms: process gets killed during warmup or after a few iterations, no obvious tensor leak in app logs, but dmesg shows GPU driver GPU page faults and then oom-killer-like messages. Happens across two different container images (one based on ubuntu:22.04 + cuda-12.1, another using cuda-11.8). Suspect version skew between libcuda (driver) installed on host and container CUDA runtime / libcudart / cuBLAS variants, plus occasional kernel module reloads after node maintenance causing NVML instability.

Observations timeline (quick):
- 2026-02-18: First report from canary: model warmup fails ~1-2 minutes after start. Container logs show CUDA out-of-memory in TRT build during initial compilation. App uses token-level batching which rapidly allocates KV cache for a 2048 context.
- 2026-02-19: Repro on dev VM with smaller model (7B) — OOM after ~120s consistently when running multi-threaded warmup. dmesg shows: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=1234, GPU has fallen off the bus" then "nvidia: GPU 0: failed to init channel: gpu-oom" (approx paraphrase)
- 2026-02-20: Swap to image with matching CUDA 11.8 runtime; still intermittent OOMs but lower frequency. Running identical workload with CPU-only config does not reproduce.

Commands tried (notes and outputs):
1) nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
   - shows GPU memory usage spikes to ~99% then nothing left; but top-level process PID still exists until crash.
2) LD_LIBRARY_PATH diagnostics:
   - inside container: ldd /usr/local/bin/python | grep cuda
     -> points to /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.12.1
   - host: ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 -> libnvidia-glcore.so.545.XX (driver version 545.36)
   -> mismatch: container runtime 12.x vs host driver 545, but 12.x typically requires >=525 so should be OK; still suspicious because we have some mixed vendor libs loaded from host mount (/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu) and container image.
3) docker run --gpus all --rm -it image:cuda12 bash
   - run sample cudaMemcpy test (deviceQuery) -> passes
   - run small TF matrix multiply with pinned memory -> OK
   - run our inference harness with --num-warmup 10 --concurrency 4: OOM after ~90s
4) dmesg snippet (copied right after crash):
   - [ 2437.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 313, pid=2345, 0(0x00000000) 0x7ffdb7d3
   - [ 2437.123467] nvidia: GPU 0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
   - [ 2437.123470] nvidia-modeset: Unloading module nvidia-modeset due to GPU removal.
   - [ 2437.123480] python[2345]: segfault at 0 ip ... rsp ...

Hypotheses (ranked quick):
- H1: Mixed ABI between host libcuda and container libcudart/cuBLAS causing kernel channel failures under high memory-pressure codepaths (compilation/trt init + KV cache growth). Some code paths allocate GPU memory via runtime and others via driver -> mismatch in expectations.
- H2: Driver bug (NVIDIA 545.x) interacting with NVLINK or multi-process MIG scheduling on this instance type causing GPU to reset under heavy small-allocation churn.
- H3: We are actually hitting real physical OOM on device because our batching policy + prefix caching exceeds available VRAM when runtime JIT compiles kernels; occasional fragmentation leaves no contiguous blocks for new allocations (observed in similar contexts on A100s with many small allocations).
- H4: Host process (system or kubelet) is forcing GPU reset because kernel sees fatal fault from one process; subsequent container restart hides root cause. Need to capture full NVML trace.

Repro attempts and toggles tried (notes):
- Reduce batch size from 8 to 4 -> reduced frequency but didn't eliminate.
- Disable TRT optimization / disable JIT / set TORCH_NVFUSER_DISABLE=1 -> runtime allocations behave differently, OOM frequency drops significantly (points toward JIT/trt compile memory spike).
- Pre-allocate KV caches earlier (reserve big allocation at start) -> seemed to make failure deterministic (fail earlier) which points to fragmentation vs absolute capacity.
- Set CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 -> no change in failure timing.
- Run inside privileged container with host /usr/lib/nvidia mounted vs clean image -> privileged + host libs lowered failure rate (makes me wonder if packaged libraries in image are not fully compatible).

Useful snippets captured:
- Python OOM stack (trim):
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "serve.py", line 102, in <module>
      model.generate(...)
  RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.05 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 29.12 GiB already allocated; 0 bytes free; 29.50 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)

- dmesg Xid 313 explanation from nvidia forums: usually memory-corruption or illegal memory access; can be triggered by driver bugs or kernel/firmware mismatch.

Next diagnostic steps (practical):
1) Collect nv-hostengine and nvlog (NVML) at time of failure: set up a background nvprof/nvml script to poll NVML memory and proc maps every 1s and persist to disk for postmortem. (script idea in linked artifacts)
2) Reproduce on staging with identical host driver and container runtime combinations: matrix test {driver 535, 545} x {cuda 11.8, 12.1} and capture dmesg + python malloc traces.
3) Try single-threaded warmup (no concurrency) to see if multi-process concurrency is a factor.
4) Build minimal repro: small program that allocates many small GPU tensors in a loop + triggers cublas/trt calls to match observed pattern (helps isolate fragmentation vs driver bug).
5) Run memtest for GPU (memtestG80-like) to exclude hardware faults — schedule node for isolated run.
6) If driver reproduces, roll node to older driver (535) on one node and push traffic; monitor for 48h.

Notes for possible mitigations (short-term):
- Add admission control: limit concurrent warmup pipelines per GPU to 1; increases cold-start time but prevents OOM spikes.
- Force pre-quantization / smaller KV cache on hosted small instances.
- Serve using model variant with lower compilation needs or warm compiled kernels in operator init under controlled memory reservation.

Related tickets / links (scratch):
- Linear: INF-4821 (canary OOMs after rollout v2026-02-17)
- Slack thread: #runbook-ooms - pinned logs
- PR to runtime with nvml poller: github.com/redwood/ops-scripts/pull/42

Open questions / things I forgot to try:
- Are there multiple libcuda versions visible in /proc/<pid>/maps at crash? (I didn't capture full maps; next run will save /proc/<pid>/maps immediately after crash)
- Does setting CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID change anything (maybe process scheduling across NUMA/PCI ordering matters)?
- Does disabling persistence mode on driver change behavior? (was left at default true on nodes)

Immediate next run plan (today):
- Deploy image with nvml poller mounted and a tiny wrapper that dumps /proc/<pid>/maps and ldconfig -p to /tmp when process exits/crashes. Keep one node isolated for iterative repro with driver 545 and cuda12 image.
- If reproducible: capture full core and run addr2line on segfault to see if fault inside nvidia module or our process.

Appendix: quick nvml poller snippet (concept):
  #!/bin/bash
  while true; do
    ts=$(date --iso-8601=ns)
    nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,index,memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu --format=csv >> /tmp/nvlog.csv
    sleep 1
  done

(Yes, not ideal but will give us a time-series to correlate with dmesg)

----
Notes-to-self: keep this doc short-lived; move triage notes into INF-4821 once we confirm driver vs runtime. If someone else picks this up, please ping me (Samira) in #runbook-ooms before changing driver across cluster to avoid cascading restarts.
